label: digit 3 as the first token of the sequence
explanation: Fires when the input at step 0 (the first original token) is the digit 3, at near-constant magnitude (~1.22, the max) on every such sequence; zero false positives on dev. It never fires on a 3 later in the original phase, on the delimiter, or in the copy phase. The only misses are weak echoes at step 1 when the step-1 input is 3: ~0.09 of max after a leading 3 (3 3 ...), ~0.03 of max after a leading c (c 3 ...). Together these hold 0.4% of activation mass. Magnitude does not vary with L or with later tokens.

issues: All claims hold. On dev, the feature fires only in the original phase (0 activations at the delimiter and in the copy phase). It fires only on in_tok 3, only at t in {0,1}, and has a max of 1.219 with a median of 1.219.
Test split: precision 1.0, recall 0.939, F1 0.969, mass recall 0.996, with 0 false positives.

The 1071 test misses are exactly the two step-1 echo classes the explanation describes. (t==1)&3&orig(0)==3 has precision 1.0 and 544 steps (~0.09 of max). (t==1)&3&orig(0)==c has precision 1.0 and 527 steps (~0.03 of max). A bare 3 at t==1 has only 6.5% precision, so the echo really does depend on the history.
The recall shortfall comes only from these tiny echoes, which the explanation already documents. They carry 0.4% of activation mass. The label is not an overclaim.
